palette.notes: Not pixel art: live-action phone footage of a LEGO brick mosaic build. Code found no palette (palette_size 0, no ramps); the final mosaic is many-coloured bricks.

lighting: Natural window light with hard leaf-shadow patterns across the white baseplates; ordinary room and workshop light elsewhere.
silhouette: No drawn characters; the maker's hands and body read against white plates and grey concrete. The 'pixel' is a 1x1 LEGO stud.

motion.timing: Live video at 30 fps: holds median 33.3 ms, 27.28 drawings/s (every frame changes). Fast-cut process montage, a new shot roughly every 1.5-2 s on the sheet.

texture: Physical stud grid of baseplates is the texture; final shot shows a dense, chunky mosaic of bricks.
camera: Handheld phone, top-down close-ups on hands and plates, a few wide shots of the maker carrying the board and painting it.

acting.enters: The maker opens by carrying a large board into the room, then the clip cuts to unboxing.
acting.acts: Hands unbox plates, sort bricks, trim plates, glue studs; the build is shown step by step.
acting.depth: Wide shots of the person alternate with tight hand close-ups; the scale jump keeps it moving.

techniques: not pixel art: physical LEGO mosaic where each stud is one pixel
process montage: unbox, sort, cut, glue, reveal
top-down hand close-ups on a flat grid
payoff withheld: the finished mosaic only appears at the end
feel: real hands + stud grid + fast cuts toward a withheld reveal = satisfying build tension (not pixel art)
for_fred: Borrow the withheld reveal, not the look: let Fred build or fetch something in quick cut steps and show the finished thing only at the end, so the reel earns its payoff.
